title: Cross-Contrastive Clustering for Multimodal Attributed Graphs with Dual Graph Filtering

problem.claim: Clustering multimodal attributed graphs is needed for practical applications involving complex entities with attributes from multiple modalities.

gap.claim: Existing multi-view clustering solutions largely rely on high cross-view attribute correlation and overlook low modality-wise correlation and intense feature-wise noise in multimodal attributes from large pretrained language and vision models, leading to suboptimal clustering performance.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report empirical studies showing that existing multi-view clustering solutions have the stated limitations and produce suboptimal clustering performance in this setting.

narrative_sequence.summary: MMAGs represent complex interconnections among entities with attributes from multiple modalities.
Clustering MMAGs supports applications such as social community detection and medical data analytics.
Existing methods overlook distinctive multimodal characteristics, including low modality-wise correlation and intense feature-wise noise, resulting in suboptimal clustering performance.

source_observation.claim: Multimodal clustering methods may perform poorly when they assume high correlation across views despite low modality-wise correlation and substantial feature-wise noise.

interpretation.claim: Method assumptions should match the statistical characteristics of representations produced by different modalities.

application.claim: When designing clustering methods for multimodal attributed graphs, explicitly account for modality-specific correlation and feature noise.

exception.claim: The supplied abstract units do not establish whether this design principle generalizes beyond the described MMAG setting.
